scope: CPU rest proportions, bone matrices, skinning and sampled face geometry attributes; no rendering or visual likeness judgement.
limitations: A procedural rig and finite continuous transforms do not establish finished character art, anatomical quality, collision avoidance, foot contact, or production topology.
Tests use 60 Hz and scene-unit thresholds; bind-space body shortening and the post-bind default uniform head enlargement are checked separately.
Face attributes are scanned in full at rest and at selected action frames, not on every frame.
No browser, application, camera, or real audio output is exercised.

checks.name: 40 actual bones and one actual SkinnedMesh
unique bones and skeleton hierarchy rooted under body
all geometry and skin attributes finite and correctly sized
valid normalized skin weights with real multi-bone blending
bind inverse matches every bone after explicit skeleton.pose
rest skinning preserves all original vertex positions
new face meshes have finite vertex attributes at rest
all 40 rest bones use the shortened-body coordinates with x/z preserved
bind head center is 1.896 with unit head/body/root scale
shortened pelvis root position is applied exactly once
tail parent chain and initial local/world transforms
moving root group preserves skin coordinates and applies world transform once
public default tuning explicitly selects body 0.74 and uniform head 1.08
default posed head is uniform 1.08 at the unchanged bind pivot
default head scale really deforms head vertices without scaling body vertices
default enlarged head and all face attributes remain finite
body shortening clamps below-range input to the explicit 0.68 minimum
non-unit headWidth 1.07 keeps skinned geometry and face finite during movement
